title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

reading.body:
This is a case of impersonation carried out at scale through a platform's paid advertising system. The ads used cloned voices and deepfake video to present themselves as banks, telecoms companies and named public figures, and they were distributed as promotions rather than as ordinary posts. The harm did not come from the synthetic media alone. It came from the combination of a convincing fabricated identity, a paid placement that lent it reach, and a call to action that moved victims off the platform to share personal details or send money.

The failure sits in the ad review and moderation layer, not in the generation of the content. The reporting notes that many ads had comments disabled and carried no AI labels, and that some linked destinations were registered abroad. Those are signals that were visible in the ad itself or in its landing page. Catching this would have required checking the advertiser's identity against the brands and people being invoked, and treating the absence of an AI label on synthetic video as a flag rather than a neutral detail.

What is not established is who placed the ads, whether any single actor was behind them, or what platform enforcement followed. The loss figures come from victims who spoke to the reporter, and the national loss estimate is attributed to NITDA. The report describes a moderation gap, and a gap is not the same as a finding of intent.

reports.title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

summary:
A Premium Times investigation found that AI-generated scam ads are running as paid promotions on TikTok in Nigeria, impersonating brands like OPay, UBA, MTN and Airtel, plus public figures such as Aliko Dangote and Tony Elumelu. Over five weeks, the reporter documented 130 such ads, many with cloned voices and deepfake videos, promising grants, giveaways and investment returns. Victims lost money after sharing personal details, including one man who lost about N150,000 and another who lost roughly N1 million in crypto.

The ads often had comments disabled and no AI labels, and some linked websites were registered abroad. TikTok's rules ban scams and impersonation, but the report says moderation gaps let them through. Nigeria loses over $500 million yearly to scams, according to NITDA. The article does not say what happens next.
